entry.title: Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say
entry.summary: A projectile hit a passenger terminal at the airport in Riyadh on Sunday, the day after a deadly missile attack on the facility carried out by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebel group killed 13 people. An unidentified projectile hit terminal 4 at King Khalid international airport, starting a fire, killing one person and injuring 11, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities. Air defences also intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of the airport. It was the latest of several attacks on the airport in the past week. The escalating attacks threatened to draw more countries into the Yemen conflict and further widen the regional fallout of the US-Iran war, which has already spread to Lebanon and Iraq. In a post on X, the British embassy in Saudi Arabia advised against all but essential travel to the cities of Jeddah and Dammam and to avoid almost all airports. After Saturday’s strike on Riyadh airport, the US president, Donald Trump, said he was weighing whether to join the Saudi military campaign in Yemen, telling reporters: “We’re going to look into it.” The Iran-allied Houthis claimed to have launched several attacks on the airport, including the attack on Saturday, which killed 13 people and injured more than 300 – the deadliest attack on a Gulf country since the war with Iran started in March and an apparent escalation in the Houthis’ war with Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government that Riyadh sponsors. In response to the attack, Saudi authorities extended the closure of the airport and said schools would be moved online until Thursday. 关键事实：A projectile hit a passenger terminal at the airport in Riyadh on Sunday；a deadly missile attack on the facility carried out by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebel group killed 13 people；An unidentified projectile hit terminal 4 at King Khalid international airport

entry.title: Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’
entry.summary: Ukrainian president earlier rejected US call for Kyiv to stop bombing oil refineries, saying Moscow must first end attacks on energy infrastructure Donald Trump has announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, apparently without consulting Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said the deal to stop long-range attacks was “news to me”. “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Donald Trump has announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, apparently without consulting Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said the deal to stop long-range attacks was “news to me”. In a social media post, the US president claimed the two sides had reached an agreement. “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” he wrote on Truth Social. He offered no further details. Zelenskyy said he was surprised by the announcement but would agree to it if Vladimir Putin did the same. “If President Trump negotiated it with Putin – please tell us when the ceasefire begins. We are ready and we will accept it,” the Ukrainian president told the Axios website. There was no sign that the Kremlin was observing Trump’s ceasefire. According to Zelenskyy, Russian drones took to the sky “throughout the day” on Sunday. There were also “unfortunately” several airstrikes, he said, including on energy infrastructure. 关键事实：Donald Trump has announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine；apparently without consulting Volodymyr Zelenskyy；who said the deal to stop long-range attacks was “news to me”

entry.title: Hormuz attacks intensify as efforts to end war on Iran stall
entry.summary: Tehran, Iran – Strikes around the strategic Strait of Hormuz have picked up again as mediated efforts to end the US-Israel war on Iran remain deadlocked. This comes as at least a dozen ships were attacked over the week ending on October 5, the highest number since the war began. At least one was hit off the north coast of Qatar, signalling that the danger extends beyond the immediate Hormuz passage as Iran and the US vie for control. US Vice President JD Vance said last week that Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to end the war, signalling a potential easing of the oft-repeated US demand that zero enrichment must take place on Iranian soil. 关键事实：This comes as at least a dozen ships were attacked over the week ending on October 5；the highest number since the war began

entry.title: Bill Gates warns cyberattacks most imminent AI threat
entry.summary: Bill Gates on Sunday warned that unregulated artificial intelligence poses a growing threat and predicted an escalation in AI-powered cyberattacks in the coming year. "The front that we'll probably see most dramatically in the next year is cyberattacks," Gates said in an interview with ABC News. entry.title: UK CAA seeking UAS expert to help integrate new airspace users
entry.summary: The UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is looking to hire an uncrewed aerial systems (UAS) expert, who would join the Airspace Regulation team as the UK looks to implement a new Airspace Modernisation Strategy. The UAS expert is needed to help integrate the demands of diverse airspace users such as UAS, eVTOL/hybrid aircraft, as well as general, military and commercial aviation, spaceports and space launch operators. They will perform regulatory oversight of the current airspace system to support the development of polices to integrate UAS and other new users, and assist in developing and implementing strategies and policies for airspace design, use or change. The UAS expert will also review and scrutinise airspace proposals from a wide range of sponsors such as operators, airports, the military and spaceports, producing objective and independent assessments of the direct and consequential airspace impacts for each proposed airspace change design. They would then lay out the conclusions of these assessments and form a key part of the CAA’s transparent decision-making process for approvals. A sound understanding of UK airspace, air traffic operations and emerging technology developments in the aviation industry is essential for the role. entry.title: Will the HomeView be Apple’s first smart home success?
entry.summary: Apple will announce a new smart home hub on Tuesday called the HomeView, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. Over the past couple of years, we’ve seen multiple reports that Apple was working on a new smart home product, but now it seems the product has a name and a launch date. Gurman described the HomeView as a Siri-powered device with a display and an A18 chip, allowing customers to control their other smart home devices. The HomeView will reportedly be available in two models — one designed for countertops and the other to be mounted on walls. This would be Apple’s most serious bet on the smart home to date, after it failed to get much traction for its HomeKit software framework or its HomePod smart speaker. Gurman reports that on Tuesday, Apple will also be unveiling updated versions of two other home devices, namely the Apple TV set-top box and the HomePod mini. Earlier this week, he said that Apple plans to announce a partnership with LG to create a smart lock, a thermostat, and a doorbell. 关键事实：Apple will announce a new smart home hub on Tuesday called the HomeView；Over the past couple of years

entry.title: Microsoft's Nadella bows to Trump's language diktat on "Super Intelligence" and uses it to attack OpenAI and Anthropic
entry.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is adopting President Trump's preferred terminology while continuing to undermine OpenAI and Anthropic. In his latest blog post, Nadella uses "Super Intelligence" instead of Artificial Intelligence. Trump had previously posted that anyone who keeps saying "Artificial Intelligence" should be considered an enemy. The rebranding of "Super Intelligence" to describe today's language models breaks with decades of scientific meaning behind the term, but the US tech elite doesn't seem to care as long as Trump gets what he wants. On substance, Nadella's latest piece goes after the supposed risks posed by model makers Anthropic and OpenAI, risks that primarily threaten Microsoft's own business. This time, he argues that companies should treat AI models like insider security threats, something Google Deepmind suggested before. "Not because they are necessarily malicious, but because any sufficiently capable actor with access to important systems can make mistakes or be compromised, and the architecture of containment and control must account for that," Nadella writes. His proposed fix is to separate intelligence from control over that intelligence. He calls for model diversity instead of dependence on a single model, complete logging of all actions, independent auditing, and the ability for humans to shut things down at any time. The most trustworthy system, he argues, isn't the one with the best model but the one where you have to trust the model the least. 关键事实：Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is adopting President Trump's preferred terminology；continuing to undermine OpenAI；In his latest blog post

entry.title: Honda Wants to Put a Robotic Lab Assistant on Future Commercial Space Stations
entry.summary: As I’m writing this I’m able to stare out into my driveway at my trusty Honda Odyssey. Most of the public’s association with Honda is through their “mobility” products - i.e. their cars. But the company has an impressive track record of other technical achievements, not the least of which has been in robotics. Now, it’s teaming up with space infrastructure firm Redwire to develop an automated laboratory support system for use on future commercial space stations. Automation will undoubtedly play a major role in future space stations, and Honda / Redwire’s offering sounds appealing with its impressive technical capabilities. But it remains to be seen if that is what the burgeoning space automation industry will rally around, or whether another option would potentially better fit the bill. But as space becomes more commercial, competition to supply the “shovels” of the next round of microgravity scientific research will undoubtedly heat up.
